title: Graph Hall algebra cohomology realization conjecture
statement:
This entry tracks **Graph Hall algebra cohomology realization conjecture**.

The realization links combinatorial Hall algebras with topological invariants and yields a new graph invariant related to, but distinct from, the Tutte polynomial.

## Latest development

The paper establishes Green-type bialgebra structures, identifies primitive elements, gives presentations, and realizes the undirected-graph Hall algebra cohomologically.

## Editorial caveat

The source is a preprint, and the broader conjectural framework is not asserted to be settled beyond the stated realization.
source_name: arXiv
references: - [Hall algebras of graphs and rooted trees](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16849) — arXiv — Lucas Toury

title: Perturbation theory for exactly solvable combinatorial problems
statement: The asymptotic behavior of a variety of combinatorial problems has now been analyzed in great detail. Here we have in mind Ulam's problem for the length of the longest increasing subsequence, the tiling problem for the Aztec diamond, the hexagon tiling problem, and the last passage percolation problem, amongst many others. In all cases, in an appropriate scaling limit, the statistical fluctuations in the systems at hand are described by random matrix theory. The asymptotic analysis, however, depends in a critical, and rigid way, on the underlying probability measures for the systems. For example, the analysis of the last passage percolation problem requires the waiting time $w_i$ at each site $i$ to be either geometrically or exponentially distributed (Johansson): if the statistics of the waiting times is neither geometric nor exponential, the analysis fails completely. What happens if the geometric distribution, say, is slightly perturbed? The challenge here is to develop an effective perturbation theory for such systems. One expects that the random matrix behavior of the fluctuations should persist. Related work on this problem has been done by Baik-Suidan and Bouchard-Martin (cf. Problem 10).
source_name: Deift - Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems (2007) (proposed by Percy Deift)

title: The universal isolated-clique conjecture for extremal uniform hypergraphs
statement:
Let $G$ be an extremal $\ell$-uniform hypergraph for Problem 13 on $n$ vertices, and let $K_{t+1}^{\ell}$ denote the complete $\ell$-uniform hypergraph on $t+1$ vertices. An **isolated copy** of $K_{t+1}^{\ell}$ is a copy having no edge intersecting it and extending outside its vertex set. **Universal isolated-clique conjecture.** If

$$
n>Ct
$$

for some absolute constant $C$, then every extremal hypergraph for Problem 13 contains an isolated copy of $K_{t+1}^{\ell}$. The theorem preceding this question establishes only the existence of an extremal hypergraph with this property for a sufficiently large $n$; whether every extremal hypergraph has it remains open.
source_name: Haorui Liu, Mei Lu and Yi Zhang, “Shadows of Uniform Hypergraphs under a Minimum Degree Condition”, arXiv:2605.02610 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

title: Polynomial-time computability of the core and corona in 2-bicritical graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a $2$-bicritical graph with two odd cycles. The **polynomial-time computability claim.** The sets **core** $\core G$ and **corona** $\corona G$ can be computed in polynomial time. This proposes an algorithmic consequence of the structural results for $2$-bicritical graphs with two odd cycles; the source does not provide evidence that the claim has been proved or disproved.
source_name: Kevin Pereyra, “Core and Corona in 2-Bicritical Odd-Bicyclic Graphs”, arXiv:2603.11419 (2026).
references:
**7 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2504.10460](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10460), [arXiv:2308.00054](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00054), [arXiv:2112.09753](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09753), [arXiv:2110.03264](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.03264), [arXiv:1912.11906](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.11906), [arXiv:1211.4049](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4049).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11419

title: The single-interval characterization of d-convex graph-nonedges
statement: Let $d\geq 1$, let $G$ be a graph, and let $F$ be a set of nonedges of $G$. For each $f\in F$, write $(G\cup(F\setminus\{f\},f))$ for the graph-nonedge pair obtained by adding the other nonedges in $F$ to $G$ while retaining $f$ as the distinguished nonedge. The pair $(G,F)$ is **$d$-convex** when it satisfies the paper's $d$-convexity condition, and a graph-nonedge pair has the **$d$-SIP** when its Cayley configuration space is single interval in dimension $d$. **The $d$-convexity conjecture.** For any dimension $d\geq 1$ and any graph $G$ with nonedge set $F$, $(G,F)$ is $d$-convex if and only if, for every $f\in F$, $(G\cup(F\setminus\{f\},f))$ has the $d$-SIP. This would give an equivalent single-interval characterization of $d$-convexity for arbitrary nonedge sets, extending the stated low-dimensional relationship between convexity and the $d$-SIP. The claim is presented as a conjecture in the paper, and no resolution is supplied here.
source_name: William Sims and Meera Sitharam, “Graphs with single interval Cayley configuration spaces in 3-dimensions”, arXiv:2409.14227 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14227

title: Gago–Coroničová-Hurajová–Madaras conjecture on low-betweenness uniform graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a **low-betweenness BUG**, meaning a betweenness-uniform graph whose betweenness value is less than $1$. Write $\overline{G}$ for its complement. **Gago–Coroničová-Hurajová–Madaras conjecture.** If $G$ is a low-betweenness BUG, then its complement $\overline{G}$ is a disjoint union of stars of the same size. This would classify the low-betweenness betweenness-uniform graphs and show that the construction from disjoint unions of equally sized stars yields all such examples. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.
source_name: Babak Ghanbari, David Hartman, Vít Jelínek, Aneta Pokorná, Robert Šámal and Pavel Valtr, “Structure of betweenness uniform graphs with low values of betweenness centrality”, arXiv:2401.00347 (2023).
references:

title: Eoh–Choi's corona-free characterization conjecture for graph grabbing
statement: Let $G$ be a graph with a weight function $w\colon V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ whose codomain is $\{0,1\}$. Let $\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$ be the family of corona products of an odd cycle and a point. A graph is **$\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$. **Eoh–Choi's conjecture.** Alice wins the graph-grabbing game if and only if $G$ is $\mathcal{C}_\text{odd}$-free. Eoh and Choi proved the forward implication under the stated $\{0,1\}$-valued weighting setting; the conjecture asserts the converse as well and remains open.
source_name: Lawrence Hollom, “On conjectures concerning the graph grabbing game”, arXiv:2311.02109 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02109

title: The asymptotic scarcity conjecture for blockwise simple permutations
statement:
For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $W_n$ be the set of permutations of size $n$, let $\operatorname{Simp}_n$ be the set of blockwise simple permutations, and define

$$
A_n=W_n\setminus\operatorname{Simp}_n,\qquad R_n=\frac{|A_n|}{|S_n|},
$$

where $S_n$ is the symmetric group. **Asymptotic scarcity conjecture.** The proportion $R_n$ tends to $0$ when $n$ tends to infinity.

Experimental checks, corroborated through $n=23$, support this asymptotic claim; the conjecture predicts that blockwise simple permutations become asymptotically negligible among all permutations.
source_name: Eli Bagno, Estrella Eisenberg, Shulamit Reches and Moriah Sigron, “Blockwise simple permutations”, arXiv:2303.13115 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13115

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2023). “His conjecture was proven in .”

title: Lusztig–Dyer combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
statement:
Let $(W_1,S_1)$ and $(W_2,S_2)$ be Coxeter systems, and let $\sigma_1,\omega_1
easymp W_1$ and $\sigma_2,\omega_2
easymp W_2$. For each pair, let $G[\sigma_i,\omega_i]$ denote the directed Bruhat interval, whose vertices are the elements between $\sigma_i$ and $\omega_i$ in Bruhat order and whose edges are the directed reflection edges. **Lusztig–Dyer's combinatorial invariance conjecture.** If $G[\sigma_1,\omega_1]$ and $G[\sigma_2,\omega_2]$ are isomorphic as directed graphs, then

$$
P_{\sigma_1,\omega_1}=P_{\sigma_2,\omega_2}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials depend only on the directed-graph structure of the Bruhat interval, and is attributed in the source to Lusztig and Dyer. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.
source_name: Maxim Gurevich and Chuijia Wang, “Parabolic recursions for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials and the hypercube decomposition”, arXiv:2303.09251 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

title: Abdollahi–Akbari–Maimani order conjecture for non-commuting graphs
statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be non-abelian finite groups. For a finite non-abelian group $K$, let $\Gamma_K$ be the graph whose vertices are the non-central elements of $K$, with two vertices adjacent when they do not commute. **Abdollahi–Akbari–Maimani order conjecture.** If

$$
\Gamma_G\cong\Gamma_H,
$$

then

$$
|G|=|H|.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether the non-commuting graph determines the order of a finite group. It is known for $p$-groups, dihedral groups, and simple groups, but remains open in general; the source also notes that it suffices to establish it for finite AC-groups.
source_name: Valentina Grazian and Carmine Monetta, “A conjecture related to the nilpotency of groups with isomorphic non-commuting graphs”, arXiv:2302.01770 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01770

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

title: Connectedness conjecture for friends-and-strangers graphs of complete bipartite graphs
statement: Let $Y$ be a graph on $n\ge 2k\ge 4$ vertices. A **$k$-bridge** is a set of $k$ edges whose deletion disconnects the graph, and it is **non-trivial** when neither resulting component is an isolated vertex. The graph $\mathsf{FS}(K_{k,n-k},Y)$ is the friends-and-strangers graph associated with the graphs $K_{k,n-k}$ and $Y$. **Connectedness conjecture.** The graph $\mathsf{FS}(K_{k,n-k},Y)$ is connected if and only if $Y$ is a connected non-bipartite graph without a non-trivial $k$-bridge and $Y\not=C_n$. This conjecture extends the established disconnectedness criterion, while the cited theorems provide only weaker sufficient conditions for connectedness; the full characterization remains open.
source_name: Lanchao Wang, Junying Lu and Yaojun Chen, “Connectedness of friends-and-strangers graphs of complete bipartite graphs and others”, arXiv:2302.00900 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00900

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

title: Maximum-minimum-dimension conjecture for tight irreducible subcube partitions
statement:
For a subcube partition $F$, let $\delta(F)$ denote the minimum dimension of a subcube in $F$. A subcube partition is **tight** if every coordinate is constrained by some subcube, and **irreducible** if no proper subset of more than one subcube has a union that is a subcube.

**Maximum-minimum-dimension conjecture.** Every tight irreducible subcube partition $F$ of length $n$ satisfies

$$
\delta(F)\leq n/2-o(n).
$$

The constructions in the paper motivate this asymptotic upper bound, but no general proof is given.
source_name: Yuval Filmus, Edward Hirsch, Sascha Kurz, Ferdinand Ihringer, Artur Riazanov, Alexander Smal and Marc Vinyals, “Irreducible subcube partitions”, arXiv:2212.14685 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.14685

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

title: Scaling conjecture for clustering in finite spatial inhomogeneous random graphs
statement:
Let $\mathbb{G}^{(n)}$ be the finite spatial inhomogeneous random graph, let $\mathrm{CC}_{\mathbb{G}^{(n)}}(k)$ denote its clustering function, and let $\gamma(k)$ denote the clustering function of the corresponding infinite SIRG. For a sequence $k_n\to\infty$, define

$$
\phi(k_n):=\begin{cases}
\frac{k_n}{\log k_n} &\text{if }\beta=a+1,\ a\in(1,\infty),\\
k_n &\text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
$$

and

$$
\psi(n):=\begin{cases}
 n^{\frac{1}{\beta-1}} &\text{if }\beta\geq (a+1)\vee 2,\ a\in[0,\infty),\\
 n^{\frac{2+a-\beta}{\beta-1}} &\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

**Scaling conjecture for finite graphs.** Consider the finite SIRG $\mathbb{G}^{(n)}$. If $\phi(k_n)=o(\psi(n))$, then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{CC}_{\mathbb{G}^{(n)}}(k_n)}{\gamma(k_n)}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1.
$$

If $\phi(k_n)=(1+o(1))\psi(n)$, then, for some $L_0,\lambda>0$,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{CC}_{\mathbb{G}^{(n)}}(k_n)}{\gamma(k_n)}\xrightarrow{d}L_0\operatorname{Poi}(\lambda).
$$

If $\phi(k_n)=\omega(\psi(n))$, then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{CC}_{\mathbb{G}^{(n)}}(k_n)}{\gamma(k_n)}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0.
$$

These conjectured limit laws describe the regimes in which the finite model follows the infinite-model clustering asymptotics, exhibits a critical Poisson-type fluctuation, or has negligible clustering relative to $\gamma(k_n)$. The conjecture is motivated by local convergence of the finite model to the infinite SIRG and the known fixed-$k$ convergence, but the simultaneous growth of $k_n$ with $n$ remains unresolved.
source_name: Remco van der Hofstad, Pim van der Hoorn and Neeladri Maitra, “Scaling of the clustering function in spatial inhomogeneous random graphs”, arXiv:2212.12885 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12885

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

title: The three-bond-dimension reduction for the bridge-graph conjecture
statement:
Let $(a,b)$ and $(a',b')$ lie in $\mathbf{U}_3\cup\mathbf{V}_3\cup\mathbf{W}_3$, and consider the bridge graph with bond dimension $3$ and boundary dimensions $a,b,b',a'$. **Three-bond-dimension reduction conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{QMinCut}=\operatorname{QMaxFlow}=\min\{a'b,ab'\}.
$$

The paper proves a reduction showing that the preceding general bridge-graph conjecture is equivalent to this specialization at $w=3$. Thus this displayed statement is the remaining three-bond-dimension case rather than an independent stronger assertion; its resolution would settle the general conjecture through the reduction.
source_name: Fulvio Gesmundo, Vladimir Lysikov and Vincent Steffan, “Quantum max-flow in the bridge graph”, arXiv:2212.09794 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09794

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

title: Visual-topology conjecture for sublinearly Morse boundaries of graph manifolds
statement: Let $G$ be the fundamental group of a non-positively curved graph manifold, let $X$ be its universal cover, and let $T_{\infty}$ be the Bass–Serre tree of the graph-of-groups decomposition. Let $\mathcal{T}(G,X,T_{\infty})$ be the topology induced by the action of $G$ on $T_{\infty}$, and let $\partial_{\kappa}X$ be the $\kappa$-Morse boundary. **Graph-manifold visual-topology conjecture.** The topology $\mathcal{T}(G,X,T_{\infty})$ coincides with the visual topology on $\partial_{\kappa}X$. The paper describes proposed approaches via curtain and median topologies, but controlling flats crossing infinitely many pieces remains an obstacle; the conjecture is open.
source_name: Carolyn Abbott and Merlin Incerti-Medici, “Hyperbolic projections and topological invariance of sublinearly Morse boundaries”, arXiv:2212.09539 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09539

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

title: The simplicity conjecture for convex hulls of signed Wachs permutations
statement:
Let $m\in\mathbb{P}$, and let $c(\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(B_{2m}))$ be the convex hull of the signed Wachs permutations in $\mathbb{R}^{2m}$. **Simplicity conjecture.** The polytope $c(\operatorname{\mathcal{W}}(B_{2m}))$ is simple.

This conjecture is part of the paper's proposed program on convex hulls of Wachs and signed Wachs permutations. The supplied text gives no verification range or resolution for the signed statement, so it remains open.
source_name: Francesco Brenti and Paolo Sentinelli, “Wachs permutations, Bruhat order and weak order”, arXiv:2212.04932 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04932

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

title: Xu's conjecture for normal Cayley graphs
statement:
Let $R$ be a group of order $r$ such that $R\not\cong \mathrm{Q}_8\times\mathrm{C}_2^m$ for any nonnegative integer $m$. For $S\subseteq R$ with $S=S^{-1}$, let $\operatorname{Cay}(R,S)$ be the Cayley graph of $R$, and call it **normal** when $R$ is normal in $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Cay}(R,S))$.

**Xu's conjecture.** The proportion of inverse-closed subsets $S$ of $R$ such that $\operatorname{Cay}(R,S)$ is a normal Cayley graph of $R$ approaches $1$ as $r$ approaches infinity.

The source explicitly says that the digraph part had been confirmed by Morris and Spiga, whereas this graph part remained open there.
source_name: Binzhou Xia and Shasha Zheng, “Asymptotic enumeration of graphical regular representations”, arXiv:2212.01875 (2023).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1911.09444](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09444).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.01875

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2022). “This conjecture has been confirmed recently by Morris and Spiga .”

title: Asymptotic upper-bound conjecture for the minimum size of k-dicritical oriented graphs
statement:
Let $o_k(n)$ be the minimum number of arcs in a $k$-dicritical oriented graph of order $n$. Suppose that, for each fixed $k$, there is a constant $c_k$ such that

$$
o_k(n)=c_k n+o(n).
$$

**Asymptotic upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
\frac{c_k}{2k-3}\rightarrow 1\quad\text{when }k\rightarrow +\infty.
$$

The paper establishes upper and lower bounds on $o_k(n)$ and proposes that the constructions giving the upper bound are nearly optimal, with the asymptotic growth rate approaching the upper bound as $k$ tends to infinity.
source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Thomas Bellitto, Frédéric Havet and Clément Rambaud, “On the minimum number of arcs in k-dicritical oriented graphs”, arXiv:2207.01051 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.01051

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

title: The general-graph extension of the estimation-error lower-bound lemma
statement:
Let $G$ satisfy the paper's general-graph regularity assumption, and let $\\{V_n\\}_{n \ge 1}$ satisfy the candidate-set assumption. For each initial source $v$, write $\mathbb{P}_v$ for probability under source $v$, let $v^*$ be the true source, let $\widehat{v}_B(t)$ be the estimator at time $t$, let $\pi(t)$ be the observation history up to time $t$, let $d$ be graph distance, and let $F_v$ denote the relevant graph-dependent time-scaling function. **General-graph estimation-error conjecture.** There are constants $a_1”=a_1”(G,Q_0,Q_1)$ and $b_1”=b_1”(G)$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{v\in V_n}\mathbb{P}_v\left(\min_{0\le t\le F_v(a_1”\log n)}\mathbb{E}_{\pi(t)}[d(v^*,\widehat{v}_B(t))]\le b_1”\cdot\mathbb{E}_{\pi(0)}[d(v^*,\widehat{v}_B(0))]\right)=0.
$$

The claim is presented as an expected extension of the paper's lower-bound lemma from regular trees and lattices to suitable general graphs; the displayed text leaves the referenced graph and candidate-set assumptions unspecified, so its precise scope and eventual status require verification.
source_name: Anirudh Sridhar and H. Vincent Poor, “Quickest Inference of Network Cascades with Noisy Information”, arXiv:2110.08115 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.08115

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

title: The graph dissimilarity metric conjecture
statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be graphs with the same number of vertices, and let $Delta$ be the dissimilarity measure obtained from the collections of horizontal homologies partitioned by the number of black-coloured vertices. **Metric conjecture.** The dissimilarity $Delta$ is a metric on the set of graphs, meaning that

$$
Delta(G_1,G_2)>0
$$

whenever $G_1\neq G_2$. The dissimilarity is already known to be a pseudometric for graphs with a fixed number of vertices; the conjecture asserts that it separates distinct graphs.
source_name: Daniele Celoria, “Filtered simplicial homology, graph dissimilarity and überhomology”, arXiv:2105.03987 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03987

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2021).

title: The DGA$_\alpha$-spectral determination conjecture for graphs in $\mathfrak{F}_n$
statement:
Let $\mathfrak{F}_n$ denote the class of graphs used in the paper, and let $n$ be the order of the graph. For $\alpha\in[0,1)$, let $c_\alpha$ be the associated parameter and let DGA$_\alpha$S mean that the graph is determined by its generalized $A_\alpha$-spectrum.

**DGA$_\alpha$-spectral determination conjecture.** If $G\in\mathfrak{F}_n$, $n$ is even, and $c_\alpha\geqslant 3$ is odd, then $G$ is DGA$_\alpha$S.

The conjecture addresses the case excluded from the paper's main theorem, which treats the arithmetic criterion for determining graphs by their generalized $A_\alpha$-spectrum. Its resolution is not provided here.
source_name: Shuchao Li and Wanting Sun, “An arithmetic criterion for graphs being determined by their generalized A_α-spectrum”, arXiv:2103.04010 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04010

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).

title: Scaling-limit conjecture for the breadth-first walk on critical Erdős–Rényi graphs
statement:
Let $\theta_n$ satisfy the scaling condition in the source, and let $X_n=(X_n(k);k=0,1,\dotsm)$ be the breadth-first walk on the random graph $\mathscr{G}_n^\theta$ constructed for the $\mathscr{G}_n$ model. The process is viewed in the Skorohod space $\mathbb{D}(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$. **Breadth-first-walk scaling-limit conjecture.** The following convergence holds:

$$
\left(\frac{1}{n^{1/3}\theta_n^2}X_n\left(\left\lfloor n^{2/3}\theta_n t\right\rfloor\right);t\ge 0\right)\Longrightarrow\left(\lambda t-\frac{1}{2}t^2;t\ge 0\right).
$$

This conjecture asks whether the breadth-first walk associated with the critical Erdős–Rényi graph has the same parabolic-drift scaling limit suggested by the continuous Lamperti transform. The paper does not establish this convergence for the breadth-first walk, so the claim remains open.
source_name: David Clancy, “A new relationship between Erdős-Rényi graphs, epidemic models and Brownian motion with parabolic drift”, arXiv:2006.06838 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.06838

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

title: Nontriviality conjecture for bucklings of spatial theta-graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a $\theta$-graph in $S^3$. A **belt** $B$ is an oriented annulus intersecting the edges of $G$ in intervals, and $G(B)$ denotes the spatial graph obtained by buckling $G$ along $B$. **Buckling nontriviality conjecture.** There is no $\theta$-graph $G$ in $S^3$ and no belt $B$ intersecting all the edges of $G$ such that $G(B)$ is either the trivial $\theta$-graph or the Kinoshita graph. This would rule out the simplest possible outcomes for buckling along a belt meeting every edge; the surrounding discussion notes that little is known about how buckling affects spatial graphs, although buckling preserves the Brunnian property when the original graph is Brunnian and the belt intersects every edge.
source_name: Scott A. Taylor, “Abstractly Planar Spatial Graphs”, arXiv:1902.01719 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.01719

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

title: Polynomial-growth conjecture for Möbius values of the permutations $\pi_{n,k}$
statement:
For $k\le n$, let $\pi_{n,k}$ be the subpermutation of $\kappa_n$ induced by the values $n+1,n+3,\dots,n+2k-1,1,3n+1,2,3n+2,\dots,n,4n,n+2,n+4,\dots,n+2k$. In particular, $\pi_{n,1}=\pi_n$. **Polynomial-growth conjecture.** For every fixed $k\ge 1$, the absolute value of the Möbius function grows as

$$
|\mu(1,\pi_{n,k})|=\Theta(n^{k^2+6k}).
$$

This refines the authors' computed example $\pi_n=\pi_{n,1}$ and is supported by their intuition and preliminary results; the source gives no proof or resolution.
source_name: Vít Jelínek, Ida Kantor, Jan Kynčl and Martin Tancer, “On the growth of the Möbius function of permutations”, arXiv:1809.05774 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.05774

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

title: The stable fixed point conjecture for target-free cliques in combinatorial threshold-linear networks
statement:
Let $G$ be a directed graph on vertex set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\sigma\subseteq[n]$. A **target-free clique** is a clique in $G$ with no common target outside the clique. The subset $\sigma$ is the support of a stable fixed point of the combinatorial threshold-linear network associated to $G$ if and only if it is a target-free clique.

**Stable fixed point conjecture.** A subset $\sigma\subseteq[n]$ is the support of a stable fixed point if and only if $\sigma$ is a target-free clique.

This conjecture extends the stated fact that target-free cliques are exactly the supports of fixed points, and that these fixed points are stable. It also includes the singleton case, where target-free cliques are precisely sinks. The surrounding discussion presents this as a conjecture based on the observed graphs; its general status is not established in the supplied text.
source_name: Katherine Morrison and Carina Curto, “Predicting neural network dynamics via graphical analysis”, arXiv:1804.01487 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

title: Dynamical splitting conjecture for shifted states on star graphs
statement:
Let $K=1$ and consider the shifted state on a star graph with shift parameter $a<0$. The graph has one incoming edge and $N-1$ outgoing edges, meeting at the vertex $x=0$; a solitary wave is a localized travelling wave of the NLS flow.

**Dynamical splitting conjecture.** In the case $K=1$, the shifted state with $a<0$ leads to a solitary wave that moves towards the vertex point at $x=0$ along the only incoming edge, splits into $N-1$ solitary waves in the $N-1$ outgoing edges, which transform due to their spectral instability while moving outward from the vertex point at $x=0$.

This conjecture records the dynamical picture suggested by the momentum balance and travelling-wave calculations. The supplied text says that the validity of this picture is beyond the scope of the work and remains to be proved.
source_name: Adilbek Kairzhan and Dmitry E. Pelinovsky, “Spectral stability of shifted states on star graphs”, arXiv:1710.01178 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.01178

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

title: Asymptotic ratio conjecture for spanning trees of suitable graphs
statement:
Let $J_{n,m}$ be the graph whose number of spanning trees is denoted by $sigma(J_{n,m})$, and let $n,m
ein\mathbb{N}$ with fixed $n\geq 2$. Define

$$
a_{n,m}=\frac{\sigma(J_{n,m+1})}{\sigma(J_{n,m})}.
$$

**Asymptotic ratio conjecture.** The limit exists:

$$
\lim_{m\to +\infty}a_{n,m}=\delta_n,
$$

where $\delta_n\in\mathbb{R}$. Moreover,

$$
\sigma(J_{n,m})=(\delta_n)^{m-3}\sigma(J_{n,3}).
$$

The conjecture proposes a limiting multiplicative growth rate for the number of spanning trees as the second graph parameter tends to infinity. The preceding numerical values suggest this behavior for $n=2$ and $n=3$, but no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.
source_name: Maurizio Imbesi, Monica La Barbiera and Santo Saraceno, “Algorithmic releases on the spanning trees of suitable graphs”, arXiv:1704.04892 (2024).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1701.08335](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.08335).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.04892

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).

title: The vertex bound conjecture for critical graphs of tree-depth k
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of tree-depth $k$, meaning that $k$ is the least number of labels in a vertex ranking of $G$ such that every path joining two vertices with the same label contains a vertex with a higher label. A graph is **critical** if it has tree-depth $k$ and every proper minor has smaller tree-depth. **Vertex bound conjecture.** Every critical graph with tree-depth $k$ has at most

$$
2^{k-1}
$$

vertices. This conjecture concerns the possible size of minor-minimal obstructions at each tree-depth; the supplied source does not state whether the bound has been proved or disproved.
source_name: Michael D. Barrus and John Sinkovic, “Classes of critical graphs for tree-depth”, arXiv:1502.05277 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.05277

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).

title: Polynomial-growth conjecture for permutations avoiding a fixed pattern
statement:
Fix a positive integer $t$. Let $\pi$ be a $k$-permutation that avoids at least one $t$-permutation, and let $L(\pi)$ denote its Stanley–Wilf limit.

**Polynomial-growth conjecture.** If $\pi$ avoids some $t$-permutation, then

$$
L(\pi)=k^{O(1)}.
$$

The paper presents this as a plausible conjecture. Its results show that containing all sufficiently large $t$-permutations forces super-polynomial growth in $k$, leaving the stated polynomial-growth regime as an open structural question.
source_name: Jacob Fox, “Stanley-Wilf limits are typically exponential”, arXiv:1310.8378 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.8378

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2013). “Seven years later, Albert et al. (see also ) disproved the conjectured bound by a bit.”

title: Du and Shi's minimum spectral radius conjecture for connected graphs
statement: Let $P_\alpha$ be a path of order $\alpha$, and form a graph by blowing up each vertex of $P_\alpha$ to a clique of order $k$. Consider connected graphs of order $k\alpha$ with independence number $\alpha$. **Du and Shi's conjecture.** The graph obtained in this way minimizes the spectral radius among all such graphs. This conjecture concerns the spectral extremal problem for connected graphs with prescribed order and independence number; the supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
source_name: Ya-Lei Jin and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “The Minimum Spectral Radius of Graphs with the Independence Number”, arXiv:1308.2075 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.2075

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2013).
